title: 4D Chicago Building Summary
description: One notable structure's front page, one file: data/summaries/<id>.json, where <id> is the structure id. AUTHORED, not derived — the summary is written from graded, sourced facts, never generated from attributes — and read by the Inspect app only through its compiled form, data/inspect/<scene>.json, which tools/compile_summaries.py --build writes at publish (never committed). A structure without one of these gets the templated fallback instead. Every visitor-facing string in the record is shown as written, so tools/compile_summaries.py --check refuses, beyond this schema: an `attested` fact with no source; an `inferred` or `reconstructed` fact with no `note` (AGENTS.md hard rule 2 and the reconstructed tier); a source id that does not resolve in data/sources/, a person id that does not resolve in the scene's people directory, a liberty id that does not resolve in data/liberties.json; a structure that does not stand in the record's scene; the length limits of design §12 (summary at most 60 words and 3 sentences, a resident's role at most 12 words, a Look-for line at most 8 words, a notable fact at most 25 words); and any id, snake_case word, file path, link or ticket number inside a visitor-facing string. Grades use the data's own ladder — attested, inferred, reconstructed — shown to a visitor as Attested, Inferred, Reconstructed.

text.description: Shown to a visitor exactly as written.

grade.description: The grade ladder of data/residents/index.json .vocabulary.grades, unchanged. `attested` needs at least one source; `inferred` and `reconstructed` need a `note` saying what the reasoning rests on or what bounded the invention. Every fact (status, built, and each item of key, residents, lookFor, notable and story) carries `grade`, and may carry `sources`, `note` and `liberty`.

sources.description: Source ids; each must resolve in data/sources/<id>.json. Never invent one.

note.description: The reasoning (inferred) or what bounded the invention (reconstructed). May reach a visitor on the Sources tab, so it is linted like every other string.

liberty.description: A liberty id in data/liberties.json, for a reconstructed fact recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md.

id.description: The structure id; the file's name. Must stand in data/sidecars/<scene>/<id>.json.

scene.description: The scene year this front page describes (data/scenes/<scene>.json).

address.description: The address line, e.g. a street number and the nearest cross street.

text.description: Still standing, or Gone with its year.

today.description: What it is now, in plain words.

phrase.description: T-3037: the build date as the sources give it, where a single year would overstate them ('between 1870 and 1876', '1864 or 1875'). `year` is its earliest year, the one the timeline places it at.

use.description: The third status chip: Home, Church, Store …

summary.description: At most 60 words and 3 sentences. Authored, never generated from attributes.

key.description: The key-facts grid (Architect, Owner, Style, Today …).

residents.description: Who lives here in the scene year. `person` must resolve in data/sidecars/<scene>/people.json; the compiled form carries the name from there.

lookFor.description: Things to look for; Show me turns the camera to `camera` and outlines `feature`.

feature.description: The feature the outline pulses on. Data, never shown.

notable.description: Notable facts. The compiler ranks them for the front page by impact: surprising x3, about a person x2, visible from the street x2, Attested x1.5.

style.description: A style-library module id: data/styles/<id>.json must exist (tools/compile_summaries.py refuses one that does not). Data, never shown; null where no module fits.

onThisHouse.description: The Design tab's numbered hotspots, 'On this house' (T-2641; design doc section 08 'Design', section 12 'Attribute table -> Design hotspots'). Each names a feature of this building a visitor can look at, with its grade. Optional: a building without it shows its own attributes, each with its grade, instead. Where `attribute` names one of the structure's sidecar attributes, the hotspot's grade must be that attribute's own confidence, so the tab and the record cannot grade one feature two ways. Where `camera` is given, tapping the hotspot turns the camera there (Show me, T-2640). These are not counted in the front page's Confidence meter: they restate what the record and the sidecar already grade.

detail.description: One line under it, at most 16 words.

attribute.description: The sidecar attribute this hotspot shows. Data, never shown.

feature.description: The feature Show me outlines. Data, never shown.

story.description: The Story tab's timeline, design to today.

era.description: The scene this entry belongs to; an entry tagged with another scene's era never renders on this one.
